title: Q3 2026 Product Roadmap, PRD Summary, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document summarizes the Q3 2026 product roadmap for Redwood Inference, including consolidated PRD highlights, high-level design specs for priority initiatives, pricing/packaging updates for hosted and Dedicated tiers, and an encapsulated release plan with rollout steps and success criteria. Audience: product, engineering, go-to-market, customer success, and executive stakeholders.

Key objectives for Q3 2026:

- Improve unit economics for hosted text generation by 20% through batching, KV-caching optimizations, and quantization profiles.
- Launch Redwood Optimize v2: automated model/quantization recommendations + workload-aware batching suggestions.
- GA: Private VPC deployment with KMS/HSM integration and audit log export.
- Deliver per-route cost attribution and token-level cost breakdown in Redwood Console.

1) Product overview and success metrics:

- Product vision alignment: make inference predictable and economical across deployments.
- Success metrics for Q3 2026 (OKRs):
  1. Reduce average token cost for top-50 customers by 20% (owner: Pricing & Infra).
  2. Increase Dedicated conversions by 25% quarter-over-quarter (owner: GTM).
  3. Achieve GA for Private deployments with 3 pilot customers (owner: Private Deployments).
  4. Reach 99.9% availability for hosted generation endpoints (SLO owner: SRE).

2) PRD summary (high-level requirements):

- Feature: Redwood Optimize v2 (auto-tuner)
  - Problem statement: Customers need automated guidance to balance latency, quality, and cost as workloads vary.
  - Primary use cases: model selection suggestions, quantization profile recommendations, batching/caching hints by route.
  - Must-have requirements:
    - R1: Recommend model + quantization profile per route based on historical token distribution and latency SLOs.
    - R2: Provide simulation of cost/latency delta for applying a recommended profile ("Preview Mode").
    - R3: One-click apply for hosted customers; guided config export for Dedicated/Private.
  - Non-functional requirements:
    - NFR1: Recommendations latency < 2s for 95th percentile.
    - NFR2: Safety: recommendations must include rollback metadata and direct link to eval results.
  - Owner: Product (Aisha Patel).

- Feature: Per-route token-level cost breakdown in Console
  - Problem: Customers cannot attribute cost to specific API routes or model versions.
  - Requirements:
    - R1: Token-level attribution by route/model/version with daily and 30d views.
    - R2: Exportable CSV and alerting when route unit cost increases > 15% week-over-week.
    - Owner: Product & Eng-Platform.

- Feature: Private VPC GA (KMS/HSM + Audit Logs)
  - Problem: Enterprise customers require on-prem-grade key management and immutable audit evidence.
  - Requirements:
    - R1: Bring-your-own-KMS integration (AWS KMS and compatible HSM API).
    - R2: Audit log export to S3-compatible endpoints and configurable retention policies.
    - R3: Deployment automation for air-gapped installs (reference Ansible/Helm docs).
    - Security: SOC2 control mapping and SSO integration.
    - Owner: Eng Private Deployments and Security.

3) Design specs and architecture notes (concise):

- Redwood Optimize v2 architecture:
  - Components: telemetry ingestion pipeline, offline model-evaluation service, recommendation engine, preview-simulator, application API.
  - Data inputs: per-route token histogram, latency percentiles, quality evals (prompt set scores), recent model variants used.
  - Output: ranked recommendations with estimated cost/latency/quality delta and confidence score.
  - Integrations: Console UI, API for "apply" action, permission checks via RBAC.
  - Scaling: recommendations computed in a serverless batch for large customers; real-time preview via cached profiles for small/medium customers.

- Per-route cost attribution implementation notes:
  - Enrich requests at ingress with route_id, model_version, and request_metadata.
  - Store token counts and cost multipliers in time-series DB (owner: Eng Platform).
  - Pre-aggregate nightly and provide API endpoints for Console graphs.
  - Alerts: use existing alerting infra; new alert rule templates provided in dashboards-and-alerts.

- Private VPC GA technical checklist:
  - KMS connectors validated against AWS KMS (CMK AES-GCM), HashiCorp Vault sealed envelopes, and HSM vendor APIs.
  - Audit log schema defined (timestamp, actor, action, resource, correlation_id, hashes).
  - End-to-end test harness for export and retention.

4) Roadmap and themes (quarter milestones):

- June 2026 (Q2 end): feature specs finalized; e2e test plans; pilot customers identified for Optimize and Private VPC.
- July 2026: Redwood Optimize beta (selected customers), per-route attribution v1 deployed to staging, pricing model draft complete.
- August 2026: Private VPC pilot deployments (2 customers), Console cost breakdown GA for hosted customers, Pricing & Packaging announced to sales.
- September 2026: Redwood Optimize GA, Private VPC GA with audit logs and KMS integration, release notes published, enablement for Sales/CS.

5) Pricing & packaging notes (hosted, Dedicated, Private):

- Hosted API pricing changes (effective 2026-08-15):
  - Text generation: introduce tiered per-token pricing with usage bands to encourage volume:
    - Tier A (0-10M tokens/month): $0.0009 / token
    - Tier B (10M-200M tokens/month): $0.00072 / token (20% discount)
    - Tier C (>200M tokens/month): custom negotiated (baseline 35% discount)
  - Embeddings: unchanged for Q3 (maintain per-embedding unit pricing).
  - Justification: expected 12–18% revenue uplift through better alignment with customer economics and increased Dedicated migrations.
  - Billing changes: introduce daily aggregation and per-route line items in invoices for customers on request.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  - New packaging: "Dedicated Performance" and "Dedicated Cost-Optimized"
    - Performance: higher guaranteed throughput, priority scheduling, SLA 99.95% availability.
    - Cost-Optimized: more aggressive packing, lower price per GPU-hour, best-effort burst capacity.
  - Contract terms: 12/24/36 month options with step-down pricing for longer commitments.
  - Sales enablement: SKU matrix and example TCO comparison template provided in sales-enablement.

- Private (VPC/on-prem):
  - Pricing: platform license + deployment fee + optional support bundle (Bronze/Silver/Gold).
  - Add-ons: extended retention for audit logs, compliance evidence bundle, air-gap install support.

6) Release plan & rollout checklist (Q3 GA cadence):

- Release staging -> canary -> GA phases. For each feature (Optimize v2, Console cost breakdown, Private VPC):
  1. Feature branch merged to release candidate.
  2. Integration tests pass (autoscaling, billing, RBAC).
  3. Internal dogfood: rollout to internal tenants and 2 friendly customers.
  4. Canary: 5% traffic split for 48 hours with error/latency monitors.
  5. Broader bake: 24–72 hour monitoring window, validate cost/latency/quality deltas.
  6. GA: announce to customers, enable opt-in, publish docs and SDK examples.

- Rollback criteria (example):
  - Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute or doubled baseline for 15 minutes.
  - Tail latency 95p increases > 30% and impacts SLOs.
  - Production cost delta > 25% unexpected for top 10 customers.

7) Metrics, telemetry, and reporting:

- Primary metrics to track post-launch:
  - Per-route token cost, model latency P50/P95/P99, errors per 1M requests, average tokens per request.
  - Adoption metrics: percent of routes using Optimize recommendations, number of customers on tiered pricing, Dedicated SKU uptake.
  - Business metrics: MRR delta attributable to pricing change, conversion rate Dedicated trials -> committed.

- Dashboards & alerts: templates added to dashboards-and-alerts (owner: Eng Platform).

8) Ownership, dependencies, and risks:

- Owners:
  - Product: Aisha Patel (overall), Priya Ghosh (Optimize), Marco Li (Console cost attribution).
  - Eng: Eng-Platform (cost telemetry), Eng-Serving-Runtime (batching and quantization runtime changes), Eng-Private-Deployments (VPC GA).
  - Security: Security team lead for Private GA and KMS integrations.
  - GTM: Sales & CS for packaging and enablement.

- Key dependencies:
  - Runtime changes for quantization-friendly paths (eng-serving-runtime).
  - Billing pipeline changes to expose per-route line items (finance-and-legal + eng-platform).
  - Pilot customers and legal contracts for Private deployments.

- Top risks and mitigations:
  - Risk: Recommendations cause quality regressions for edge prompts. Mitigation: Preview Mode, manual eval sets, and 2-step apply with rollback.
  - Risk: Pricing changes create churn. Mitigation: grandfathering for existing customers for 6 months and clear TCO examples.
  - Risk: KMS/HSM integration complexity. Mitigation: limit initial GA to AWS KMS + Vault patterns, expand vendors after first pilot.

9) Customer enablement and docs:

- Deliverables:
  - Updated Console UX walkthroughs, API docs (examples for apply/revert Optimize recommendations), pricing FAQ and TCO calculator.
  - Sales playbook: Dedicated SKU matrix, example contract language, negotiation guardrails.
  - CS runbook: onboarding checklist for Private deployments and pilot evaluation script.

10) Next steps / immediate actions (timebound):

- By 2026-07-01: finalize pricing tables and publish internal pricing memo for Sales. Owner: Finance & GTM.
- By 2026-07-15: Redwood Optimize beta rollout to pilot customers. Owner: Product & Eng.
- By 2026-08-01: Console per-route cost breakdown v1 GA for hosted customers. Owner: Eng Platform.
- By 2026-09-01: Private VPC GA with KMS & Audit logs. Owner: Eng Private Deployments & Security.

Appendix: release notes summary (for public release):

- Redwood Optimize v2 (GA): automated model & quantization recommendations, preview mode, and one-click apply for hosted customers.
- Console: per-route token-level cost breakdown and exportable billing CSVs.
- Private VPC: GA with AWS KMS support and audit log export.
- Pricing: tiered per-token pricing for hosted text generation (effective 2026-08-15).

For questions or to volunteer for pilot programs, contact Aisha Patel (product) or join the #prod-roadmap Slack channel.
